steps.speaker: Participant A
steps.content: 330 million!

steps.speaker: Participant B
steps.content: 350 million!

steps.speaker: Participant C
steps.content: 375 million!
The auction goes full steam ahead without the piloting of the auctioneer. Every eye in the room is glued to the burning painting.
You can't figure out why the burning painting holds such an appeal for the bidders. But there's no doubt that the hall is at breaking point.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: 375 million, going once...

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: My dear friends, you're witnessing the birth of a legend. Two misfortunes, and now we have a truth that will never be revealed...
McQueen delivers a pretentious speech to the hysterical crowd.
Everyone is caught up in the whirlpool of madness.
Numbers, now meaningless, continue to flow in the air. Some bidders even start hurling curses and exchanging blows.
Chaos reigns. Some bidders rush onto stage, jostling for the half of the second painting that hasn't been consumed by the fire, and for the shreds from the first painting on the floor.
You can't allow the M-value in the hall to climb further. You intend to push your way through the crowd, and put an end to the madness by controlling McQueen with the shackles.
But you're stopped by Maureen.

steps.speaker: Maureen
steps.content: If it's meant to be, it's meant to be. Whatever you're going to do, it won't change anything.
As Maureen makes the request, her restraining hand on your arm trembles.

options: Is this what you really want?

steps.content: It's not the painting that's being auctioned here. It's a made-up story; it's your dignity and reputation.
Once the deal is made, the name Maureen will forever be reduced to a business gimmick, and no one will ever care what you're painting.

steps.speaker: Maureen
steps.content: Creating forgeries for fame and fortune... I'm already in the game.

But your dream isn't completely dead yet, right? If it was...
you wouldn't be crying.
Maureen lets go of your arm.

steps.speaker: Maureen
steps.content: Regret... What difference does it make? I'm a greedy, obnoxious human being. I don't deserve to be saved.
Whether you deserve to be saved or not, that's for me to decide.
Maureen is dumbfounded. She watches as you determinedly push your way through the crowd toward the podium where McQueen stands.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Want to join the party, Chief? Oh, my dear, you've finally come to your senses.
You ignore McQueen's teasing remark and shove the guests holding their bid cards out of the way.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: There's nothing shameful about pursuing fame and fortune. Like I said, the sweetness of fame and fortune, once you've tasted it, is hard to let go of.
That's not true. We all make mistakes. It's just that most people don't have a second chance to make things right.
You are blindsided by another swarm of lunatics jockeying to get their hands on the painting first, but manage to squeeze past.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Do you know how it feels to squash your own dream, to be consumed by self-pity and self-negation, unable to see your future because you're blinded by pain and regret?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Not everyone is a saint like you. What's wrong with bowing down to reality and joining the decadent club?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: If they choose to sink into the mire of decadence with me, they can have all the fun in the world, day and night. Nothing wrong with that, right?
McQueen inches toward you, her eyes fixed on you. It seems to you that she's trying to persuade you to give up on Maureen, but you are not entirely sure.
I'm not a saint. Since I became Chief of the MBCC, I've made many wrong decisions, and hurt many people around me.
As long as we have the courage to confront and rectify our mistakes, we will be able to move on with our lives.
We don't have a time machine. We can't travel back in time and change the past. But at least we have some control over the future.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: ...Easy said than done. You can't possibly expect her to change her appearance and name, and go through hell all over again in this rotten vanity fair?
How can you be so sure that change is impossible when you don't know what the future looks like?
What she... she and you need is the courage to let go of the past and a chance to make better choices.
I'm going to give you both!
You push against the dense crowd with all your strength, trying to get through. But you're no match for the hysterical guests.
You're running out of energy when you feel a push from behind.
Finally, you stumble on stage and stand in front of McQueen.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: ...What a sorry sight you are! You're going through all this just so you can save Maureen? You're kind-hearted as ever, Chief.
Not just Maureen.
You snatch the candlestick from McQueen's hand and light the other corner of the painting. The old fire and new fire march toward each other, consuming the remains of the painting as they go.
You can't find the courage to leave your past behind, to conquer the fear that stems from your experience of creating and selling forgeries. Then I'll help you reduce your appalling past to ashes.
The painting is reduced to ashes in the raging fire, to the dismay of the gaping crowd.
The ash dances in currents of hot air and then spreads across the hall.
A deadly silence falls. It's so quiet that you can hear the sound of some guests swallowing hard.
...400 million DisCoins' worth of flying ash... It's surprisingly beautiful.
Only McQueen reacts to your lame joke. Everyone else is gazing at the last scrap of canvas with dark brown edges. McQueen's gaze, on the other hand, has never left you.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Y-you are simply incredible!
She shakes her head, wearing a smile.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: You burned the auction item and humiliated all the moguls here. Now they have to go home empty-handed.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: How are you gonna handle the consequences? Have you thought about that?
You are struck dumb by McQueen's remark, which also arouses anger among the crowd.
With a sizzling sound, drops of burning melted wax land on the shreds from the first painting, which then burst into flame. The fire spreads, and the anger of the 100-odd guests grows.

steps.speaker: Participant A
steps.content: Fire! Put it Out!

steps.speaker: Participant B
steps.content: My painting! My glorious damaged painting! My chance to become famous among the collectors!

steps.speaker: Participant C
steps.content: I even borrowed money for this auction!

steps.speaker: Participant
steps.content: That gray-haired scumbag! He ruined art!
steps.female_content: That gray-haired scumbag! She ruined art!

steps.content: The hall is in chaos. Some guests are running around screaming, and more are rushing toward the stage to get at you.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: What are you still doing here? Waiting for them to tear you to ribbons?
McQueen shields you behind her and takes a few steps back. Then she takes hold of a length of rope attached to the curtain.
To your surprise, the rope moves, hauling you and McQueen up.
Is this...?!

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: A replica I made of the ingenious creation by two crafty creatures from Eastside.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: And needless to say, it's as good as the original.
Why did you put such a thing in place? You knew it'd come to this?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: I've got a lot of enemies in Eastside. I always make preparations for a quick getaway.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Besides, I will never allow myself to get the Chief into trouble with me.
Amid a torrent of abuse and curses, McQueen breaks free from the crowd, taking you along. The two of you then escape through the lighting control room.
The fire rages on; black smoke hangs thick in the air. Coughing and howling, the guests go around the preparation room to pursue you.
Here!
A familiar voice comes from a dark corner.

steps.speaker: Maureen
steps.content: I'll stall them. You go first. You too, Miss McQueen.
What about you?

steps.speaker: Maureen
steps.content: Don't worry. They're not coming after me. I'm gonna be fine, and...

steps.speaker: Maureen
steps.content: Thank you. Maybe, I can be courageous, too...
Maureen points the oncoming mob in the wrong direction, as you and McQueen go through the back entrance, hastening to meet up with the MBCC reinforcements.
Maureen, she...

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: You're worried about Maureen's safety even while running for your own life. Chief, you're very kind-hearted indeed!
McQueen trots ahead, pulling you along. She looks slightly sulky.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: You're concerned about her. Have you thought about what you will do if she chooses not to turn over a new leaf?
If she chooses not to change, then I will give her another chance.
She gave me a push from behind to help me get on the stage. I know she's already made the right choice.
McQueen narrows her eyes at you, an amused look on her face that you can't quite wrap your head around.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Everyone in the MBCC says you're smart as a whip. But I think you can be infuriatingly dumb sometimes.
What do you mean?

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: You're a holder of the shackles. Don't tell me you don't know what my power is as a Sinner.
Replication... clone?
So the person who gave me a hand was...
Before you can finish your question, McQueen hops on the MBCC vehicle that's come to your rescue, pulling you on with her. The vehicle revs and speeds away, leaving the fuming building in the dust.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Why the frown? We've escaped unscathed.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Are you worried about the people caught in the fire, or Maureen?
The fire's controllable; I noticed this when we escaped. The MBCC could help contain the fire in time, and the Eastside fire department should be there soon.
As for Maureen, I've said everything needed to be said. I can only wait and see if she'll be able to pick up the paintbrush and paint again.
I frowned, because I was thinking about something you said.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Oh, really? What romantic words have I said that has got you so hooked?
...You said the art world is rotten, and the people in it aren't worth changing.
I saw for myself today how rotten the art world is. As for the second half of your statement... I proved you wrong today.
It's not as hard as you imagined to leave a tainted past behind, make new choices, and start over.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: You want me to stop seducing people to sell their dignity by creating forgeries?
Yes.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content:
I will stop, of course.
I'm one of the Sinners under the MBCC's control now. I'll do your bidding, Chief. I will do whatever you ask me to do.
She readily consents to your request, but she is wearing a secretive smile on her face.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Suppose, I mean hypothetically, Jennie decided to shoot straight. What then? She could just be an exception. You have no way of knowing that all the other once-dishonest painters wouldn't give up their dreams again for fame and fortune.
I understand that you don't believe there are many artists who have real dreams, because you were deceived and hurt by people from the profession.
But there can be many exceptions in a group. Give them a second chance, help them find courage, and they can still get back on track.
Jennie... she can be one of the exceptions.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Here we go again. Still trying to straighten me out, huh? Chief, you're so fixated on me. You want to be responsible for me all the way?
McQueen knows that you won't answer her ludicrous question. She puts up her right hand, with the fingers close together, against the sunlight that comes through the window.
The sunlight is glaring, but not a single ray of light can pass through her black-gloved hand.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: Ahahahaha!
McQueen bursts into laughter without warning. When she's done, she leans back in her seat, as if tired out.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: It'd be nice if Jennie got to choose again...

steps.speaker: Collector A
steps.content: A hardworking painter. Unfortunately, diligence is not a good selling point.

steps.speaker: Collector B
steps.content: Jennie? Never heard of her. Nice painting though. You can't be a successful artist without knowing how to publicize your works. This one didn't even bother to take out an ad.

steps.speaker: Lisa
steps.content: Pfft, they have no taste. They don't know anything about art; they should shut their mouths. It's easy to see that this painting conveys something more profound than those absurdly expensive masterpieces that have just come out.

steps.speaker: Lisa
steps.content: It's a great shame that conscientiousness might become her downfall. Conventional techniques are an impediment to her artistic expression.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're right. It's rare to find a young artist with such a great talent for artistic expression in Eastside.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Instead of putting her down, belittling her because her paintings might not sell, they should give her a chance to try new things, right?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: One day...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Her paintings will appear in the main exhibition hall of the art museum.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: One day...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Her paintings will appear in the main exhibition hall of the art museum.

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: How I wish...

steps.speaker: McQueen
steps.content: That Jennie hadn't met McQueen back then, but someone else.
